main_text.p: negavero, quin in continenti, ea averti possit, adeoq; adversarius iniquus repelli.) Non hęc, quia secundum adversarios, non defendunt, sed reparant, vindicant injuriam illatam, idque citra necessitatem, idque propria auctoritate.

Objic.7. Licitum non solum1.veluti. de jure civili vim corpori illa-3.D. de Iust. & iur.tam propulsare, sed etiam quamcunque injuriam. Respondeo enim, non agi in d. l. de injuria aliqua verbis, aut gesticulatione illata, quasi liceat injuriam non tantum verbis injuriosis, sed & alio remedio illi damno proportionato repellere. Verùm de injuria corpori illata, idque per violentam aliquam invasionem. Quod ipsum satis indicant verba d.l. subsequentia. Nam jure hoc evenit, ut quod quisque ob tutelam corporis sui fecerit, jure fecisse existimetur.

page.notes: The note mark "1" after "solum" is not clearly visible on the scan; the note "1.veluti." is placed beside that line. The word at the line break after "illa-" is read as "tam" from the sense of the passage (illatam); the scan is small. The "3.D. de Iust. & iur." note spans two lines beside "de jure civili" and "ram/tam". The word after "Non" reads "hęc" as printed. The running head is "De Duellis." and the page number "275" is printed at the top right.
